articles.title_orig: Democrats to attend Cop31 climate talks boosted by midterms and eager to make up for Trump-era setbacks
articles.title_zh: Democrats to attend Cop31 climate talks boosted by midterms and eager to make up for Trump-era setbacks
articles.content_orig:
US government will have no official presence at UN’s annual climate summit, this year’s Cop31 held in Antalya, Turkey
T he US will be absent from key UN climate talks that start on Monday, a further sign of Donald Trump’s scornful dismissal of the climate crisis. But Democrats’ crushing win in the US midterm elections has delivered a timely shot of optimism to countries now looking beyond the Trump era of climate obstruction.
For the second year in a row , there will be no official US government presence at the annual climate summit, this year known as Cop31 and held in Antalya, Turkey. While almost every other country in the world sends delegations to the talks, Trump has derided the climate crisis as a “hoax” and “bullshit” and triggered the withdrawal of the US from the entire international climate framework.
“This summit rejects reality by failing to acknowledge that extremist climate policies are destroying countries around the world,” a White House official said, confirming that the administration would not send anyone to Cop31 .
The snub is so severe that about 20 members of the US Congress heading to the summit have been denied usual state department assistance, requiring them to turn to philanthropic funding for the trip. “I’m glad we found a way to get there, but it is insane,” said Sean Casten, a Democratic congressman who is attending Cop31. “We have a lot of rebuilding to do. It hinges on Congress to maintain diplomatic continuities at Cop and minimize the damage until adults are back in the White House.”
Trump’s active support of fossil fuels , evisceration of pollution limits and throttling of clean energy projects has caused the US to become an outlier among wealthy countries, a recent UN report found . While all the other 20 major economies reduced or slowed their carbon pollution last year, the US was a “major exception” by emitting an extra 133m tons of planet-heating gases from the burning of coal, oil and gas, the report states.
Despite the world rapidly surging past “safe” temperature thresholds because of such pollution, and escalating heatwaves , floods , droughts and other calamities , Trump has remained defiant. “If you don’t get away from this green scam, your country is going to fail,” the US president told other world leaders at the UN last year, adding that the climate crisis was “the greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world”.
But the Democrats’ stunning success in the midterms last week, wresting control from Trump’s Republicans in both the House of Representatives and the Senate, has buoyed delegates gathering in Antalya. While this will be the last Cop with the US as an official party, after Trump exited the UN framework, the midterms have raised international confidence of a looming return and new, post-Trump chapter.
“This marks the beginning of the end of the Trump era,” said Mohamed Adow, director of Power Shift Africa. “His grip on Congress has been broken and hopefully paves the way for a Democratic president in two years. For everyone fighting for a livable planet, this is a moment of renewed hope.”
Trump has done “enormous damage” to the climate but the midterms results, along with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s recent electoral victory in Brazil , provides a major tonic, Adow said. “It opens the door to America returning to the climate fight with the seriousness its responsibility demands,” he said, adding that Cop31 would be the “perfect time to accelerate climate action and turn the tide on the Trump dark ages”.
US lawmakers arriving at Cop, all of them Democrats, are aware the world has long been subjected to wildly erratic US commitment to climate action, Casten acknowledged. “We go in with a fair amount of humility – as important as we are, the US has been an extremely unreliable partner on climate,” he said. “But going to Cop on the heels of these results feels a lot better. It can be a much more positive process now.”
Spanning two weeks of negotiations among 197 countries with an accompanying trade show-like jamboree of pavilions and side events interspersed by protests, the sprawling Cop process requires a sense of momentum. The electoral revolt in the US, the world’s largest historical emitter of greenhouse gases, should provide such a fillip, according to Susan Biniaz, a former longtime climate negotiator for the US at Cop.
“Much of the world is looking to the midterms for some kind of signal from the US electorate that they are unhappy with this administration,” Biniaz said. “This could elevate the mood. I don’t think the midterm elections will directly affect federal climate policy but they will help the spirit of the Cop.”
“There’s been a big shift since the midterms. I’m certainly more optimistic,” said Catherine McKenna, former environment minister of Canada. “Negotiations at Cop are important but it’s more important what happens at home and Trump has been incredibly disruptive. We will now have more Democrats acting on climate and talking about the solutions that will actually save people money.”
But what will a thumping Democratic majority in Congress be able to do on climate? Sweeping climate legislation, similar in scale to the Inflation Reduction Act signed by Joe Biden that was subsequently gutted by Republicans, is not likely given Trump’s veto power. Still, Democrats are exploring other avenues.
Investigative and subpoena powers will be used to probe parts of the administration, such as the Environmental Protection Agency, over staff cuts and what Democrats call the “unlawful” withholding of climate and clean energy spending. Trump’s attempt to pressure Europe into taking US gas will be scrutinized, as will the vulnerability of the insurance industry to the climate crisis and concerns over the US ceding clean tech industries to China.
Democrats will dominate the budget process and will likely reverse funding cuts to environmental programs and rein in datacenters, which have become highly contentious with the US public.
Some legislation, such as the speeding up of the permitting process to allow new clean energy production and transmission, may be possible with Republican support too. The midterms also delivered striking Democratic wins at the state level, bringing new governors to states such as Texas and Georgia, meaning widespread state-based action to shift away from fossil fuels will be possible.
Much of this will likely be framed as helping tackle the rising cost of living or government corruption, rather than the climate crisis itself. Some activists have criticized Democrats for so-called “climate hushing” even as most people in the US favor the end of the fossil fuel era, but Casten said emissions reductions will matter more to the new Congress than rhetoric.
“We are going to do everything – oversight, legislation and action through the courts,” he said. “There are things around the cost of gas, or housing and insurance that are climate conversations even if we don’t mention climate. It’s our job to understand how all those things are connected but we have to talk about climate change to people in a way that is salient to them. It’s not that we don’t want to talk about climate change at all.”
Regardless of how Democrats talk about the climate crisis, its effects are mounting . Scientists have warned, repeatedly, that sluggish progress in cutting emissions has left little time to avoid disastrous impacts.
The world is already set to overshoot the internationally agreed target of limiting the global temperature rise to 1.5C, locking in turmoil for people, wildlife and ecosystems around the world, and any lingering embrace of fossil fuels by major emitters like the US will only worsen this pain. When Democrats take over Congress in January, advocates will clamor for them to rapidly make up for lost time.

articles.title_zh: Russia-Ukraine war: Nine Zimbabweans caught trying to leave South Africa to join conflict
articles.content_orig:
Nine Zimbabweans have been arrested in South Africa after they were caught allegedly trying to leave the country to fight in the war between Russia and the Ukraine, police say.
The group, aged between 20 and 26, were arrested in and around Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team on Sunday evening.
They were caught as they were "preparing to board flights out of the country", authorities added, but their final destination is unclear.
They have been charged with contravening South Africa's Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which outlaws mercenary activity without government permission.
Police said five people were arrested at South Africa's biggest airport, OR Tambo, and another four at a hotel in Bruma, east of Johannesburg by a multidisciplinary team that involved Interpol.
All nine later appeared in court, according to state prosecutors.
The police statement added that the involvement of Interpol and other international law enforcement agencies indicated that the suspects had also allegedly violated laws in their respective home countries, prompting cooperation with South African authorities.
They have also not said whether the group allegedly intended to fight for Russia or Ukraine nor provided details of the organisations allegedly involved in facilitating their travel.
Citizens of several African countries, including Kenya, Ghana and South Africa, have gone to fight for Russia in Ukraine - some they had been duped and had not realised where they were going.
A Ukrainian intelligence assessment estimated earlier this year that more than 1,700 people from 36 countries in Africa have been recruited to fight for Russia.
Kenya at the time estimated that 252 citizens had been illegally conscripted in Russia. In March, Foreign Minister Musalia Mudavadi visited Moscow to address the issue.
He said at the time that an agreement had been reached to stop recruiting Kenyan nationals.
In March, Zimbabwe said that 15 of its nationals had been killed after being recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine, with more than 60 still trapped on the frontlines.
The previous month, South Africa secured the return of 17 South Africans who were allegedly tricked into joining the war.
In December last year, South African authorities arrested five people, including a journalist, for allegedly recruiting people to join the war.
Ukraine has also been recruiting foreign nationals, including from Africa.

AI’s power crunch has become so acute that Anthropic, a company that has generally avoided buying physical infrastructure, is spending $3.4 billion on natural gas turbines.
The AI company, which is planning to go public this year, is buying Caterpillar generators that equipment supplier OnePWR had originally ordered, according to a Financial Times report . The generators are capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts of electricity.
Historically, Anthropic has preferred to rent rather than buy. The company disclosed in its S-1 filing in May that it is paying SpaceX subsidiary xAI $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 to use xAI’s computing power.
“We expect to enter into additional similar services contracts,” Anthropic stated in the filing, meaning more deals to rent computing power.
But as demand for compute ramps up, the market for power has also grown increasingly uncertain, which may have forced its hand. The backlog for natural gas turbines stretches into the early 2030s, and queues to connect to the electrical grid can be just as long.
Anthropic’s purchase looks like a last resort.
According to the report, OnePWR ordered the turbines a couple years ago but couldn’t find financing to complete the purchase. Anthropic had planned to buy them from OnePWR but instead went directly to Caterpillar, the manufacturer.
It’s not clear why OnePWR was unable to secure financing despite Anthropic’s apparent interest as a customer. Whatever the case, Anthropic likely wanted to keep the generating capacity to itself rather than give a competitor an opportunity to snap it up.
AI companies have been ramping up their purchases of natural gas equipment and supplies in recent years. Google , Amazon , Microsoft , and Meta have all announced plans to build massive natural gas power plants to power their data centers on-site, rather than drawing from the public grid.
The binge has given a second wind to fracking , the drilling method used to extract natural gas from underground rock. And if the buildout proceeds as planned, U.S. data centers alone could consume more natural gas than Germany and Japan combined by 2035. The reliance on natural gas also exposes hyperscalers to price fluctuations. One analyst expects that prices could more than triple by the end of the decade in some markets. If that happens, Anthropic might have a serious case of buyer’s remorse.

articles.title_orig: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
articles.title_zh: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
articles.content_orig:
France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions "at the European level".
Iran is yet to respond to Barrot's allegations.
The cyber-attack last month saw fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France heated up, which spoilt fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.
Then last week, dozens of supermarkets across several other European countries were also impacted by a cyber-attack that targeted fridges and freezers. It is not known if the instances are linked.
Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people".
He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act".
France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added.
Separately on Monday, the Paris prosecutor said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as well as his two deputies.
Laure Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC.
Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime.
On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets.
More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight.
Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.
The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.
Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe.
Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.
Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.
Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects.
In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them.
The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations.

While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, the company has no illusions that it’s keeping pace with its rivals.
Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months. One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Those capabilities are expected to land with iOS 27.3. The bigger change, integration with third-party apps, is likely to land later, in the Spring, according to Gurman. That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example.
But that’s just the start. Apple is expected to push Siri to become more agentic and enable features that will allow it to perform ongoing tasks, not just one-offs. Gurman says:
Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step. Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.

articles.title_orig: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
articles.title_zh: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
articles.content_orig:
Poundland is unable to buy new stock to fill its shelves after being blocked by its owners from accessing cash in its bank accounts.
The discount chain is on the brink of collapse with one insider describing it as "running on fumes". It has until Thursday to secure a rescue deal.
About £50m has been frozen by its American owner Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning its 600 shops are running out of stock.
Pressure is building on Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, after the owner rejected a takeover bid that could have saved the thousands of jobs currently at risk. Gordon Brothers has been approached for comment.
Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until Thursday.
Access to funds was limited because of a tension between Gordon Brothers' dual role as both creditor and shareholder, a source said, but added they expected a relaxation of funds in the next two days.
Last week, Poundland boss Barry Williams told staff like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4% last week, which included Halloween, but said this was £1.5m ahead of budget.
He said the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where the business made losses of £68m.
The latest annual accounts have yet to be audited.
However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture of the business, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading".
It said it had provided significant funding to support the company's ability to trade since it acquired the business.
It has also made £18m, from a combination of debt interest payments and other fees and charges.
On Wednesday, executives from Gordon Brothers will appear before the Business Select Committee with MPs probing whether they are genuinely pursuing a solvent rescue of the business, which has 11,000 employees, and whether every realistic step is being taken to protect jobs and stores.
The session is being held in private given commercially sensitive discussions are still under way with bidders.
On Thursday, the 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended.
If not, Poundland is set to collapse into administration and could be broken up.
A source familiar with the sales process said London-based Xyra Group was making "significant progress" in its last minute bid to buy Poundland and could now be the front runner.
An extension of Thursday's deadline now seems an increasingly likely scenario. But such a case would be difficult to put forward if Gordon Brothers continues to block funding.
One observer remarked "if Gordon Brothers is going in front of that committee, you don't want to be giving the message we're pulling up the drawbridge".
Even if a deal is agreed to sell the business as a whole, there is no guarantee a new owner would not reduce the number of stores, but suppliers to Poundland would prefer that outcome to hundreds of sites being sold off to other retailers.
There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up stores which could mean continuing employment for many workers.
The central issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland trading as a national chain.

A top executive at one of the world's largest hedge funds is leaving her job in the U.S. to become the CEO of one of the Carney government's hallmark projects.
On Monday, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) announced that Karen Karniol-Tambour will become the CEO of Canada's nascent sovereign wealth fund.
A news release from the PMO said Karniol-Tambour has Canadian citizenship, though public records indicate she was born in Israel and has spent her professional career in the United States.
Her LinkedIn page says she has been at Bridgewater Associates for more than 20 years and rose to be co-chief investment officer. She graduated from Princeton University in 2006.

The financial magazine Barron's has named Karniol-Tambour in its list of the 100 most influential women in U.S. finance for the last seven years. She was also featured by Forbes .
At the helm of the new sovereign wealth fund, she will be tasked with identifying and investing in domestic projects with the goal of generating returns for investors and reinvesting them in new Canadian projects.
The federal government announced plans to create the fund, which it is calling the Canada Strong Fund, last spring. It has earmarked $25 billion in seed funding and committed to putting commercial asset revenue into the fund. Its goal is to finance "nation-building" projects while allowing Canadians to benefit from the returns.
The fund will also include a "retail" element for ordinary Canadians to be able to buy in directly . Last week's federal budget said those investments will take the form of notes similar to savings bonds, but details on when or how that will roll out haven't been announced.
"Under Ms. Karniol-Tambour’s leadership, the Canada Strong Fund will be professionally managed, operating at arm's length from the government, with its own board of directors," said the Prime Minister's Office.
"Together, the fund and its retail offering will create a new model of Canadian ownership, helping build national wealth while ensuring more Canadians share in the benefits of economic growth."

articles.title_orig: Sony’s new PlayStation Portal handheld includes ‘additional’ internal storage
articles.title_zh: Sony’s new PlayStation Portal handheld includes ‘additional’ internal storage
articles.content_orig:
While Sony has largely given up on the handheld market following the death of the now-lamented PlayStation Vita, the company is taking another swing at the PlayStation Portal. Following in Nintendo’s footsteps, Sony will release a Japan-only version of its handheld. The specs are mostly unchanged: the region-locked Portal will have the same 1080p LCD screen and will still be built around remotely accessing a PS5 to play games.
The big difference is that this version will have internal storage. Because of this added hard drive, the region-locked Portal will cost the same as the global model in Japan, 39,980 yen ($252). Like the Japan-exclusive PS5, it's in Midnight Black.
The PlayStation Portal's main selling point is that it lets users remotely stream games from their PS5 while connected to the same Wi-Fi as the console, so the base version doesn’t really need built-in storage. Adding a hard drive suggests the new version may eventually do more than stream; the product description says Sony included it “with an eye towards future functionality.” It’s unclear if that future functionality is for the PlayStation 5 or for the presumed PlayStation 6.
It isn’t surprising that Sony is releasing a Japan-only PlayStation Portal. The company previously took this approach with the PlayStation 5 , releasing a region-locked version of the console for the equivalent of $350. Much like Nintendo released a Japan-only version of the Switch 2, Sony did this to make the system more accessible to domestic customers amid the yen’s declining purchasing power.
The PlayStation Portal sold reasonably well despite its seemingly limited use case, moving an estimated 420,000 units in the U.S. alone within its first year. However, critics had mixed reactions . While it was praised for its build and screen quality, many reviews found that even mild connection issues had a huge impact on gameplay. The system’s streaming-only design, combined with a $199.99 price point, made it a fairly niche device.
That said, Sony has improved the system's software over the years, adding better streaming settings for those with beefy home networks.
Perhaps the device's biggest change is that Sony eventually added cloud gaming support , meaning the device was no longer restricted to PS5 owners. This lets users play any game with PS Plus cloud support, as long as they have a PS Plus Premium subscription (which costs $159.99 a year). As hardware prices continue to rise due to an ongoing RAM shortage , console manufacturers may make another significant push for cloud gaming in the near future, with this revived PlayStation Portal being Sony's first major stab.

articles.title_orig: Honda to invest $3 billion in new vehicle assembly plant in Ohio
articles.title_zh: Honda to invest $3 billion in new vehicle assembly plant in Ohio
articles.content_orig:
MARYSVILLE, Ohio — Honda Motor plans to invest $3 billion to build a new vehicle assembly plant in Ohio, the automaker announced Monday.
Honda said the new plant, which will be near its other facilities in Marysville, Ohio, is expected to begin production in 2029, have a capacity for 240,000 vehicles annually and create more than 2,000 jobs.
The facility is expected to be capable of producing traditional vehicles with internal combustion engines, all-electric vehicles and hybrid models, which have been growing in popularity in the U.S.
The plant is expected to increase Honda's light-duty vehicle capacity to 1.3 million units annually in the U.S. It currently has 12 manufacturing plants in United States, eight of which produce engines or light-duty vehicles for the auto industry.
It's the company's first new mass production U.S. vehicle assembly plant since it opened a facility in Indiana in 2008. It also opened a $70 million performance vehicle facility in 2016 and a multibillion-dollar joint venture battery plant earlier this year, both in Ohio.
"This is not simply an investment in another plant. It is an investment in the future of Honda manufacturing in America," Bob Nelson, executive vice president of American Honda Motor, said during the announcement at the company's U.S. heritage center in Ohio.
The auto industry has been trying to localize more production amid President Donald Trump 's tariffs and inflated logistics costs that have cut into profits.
Honda's plans for a new plant come roughly two weeks after Volkswagen-owned luxury brand Audi announced it would invest more than $4 billion in its first U.S. manufacturing facility in Georgia.
Detroit automakers General Motors and Ford Motor and international automakers Toyota Motor and Hyundai Motor also recently said they will spend billions of dollars on new or updated U.S. facilities.
Honda's announcement comes after the automaker in May indefinitely suspended an $11 billion investment plan to produce all-electric vehicles and batteries in Canada. It also canceled three planned EVs for the U.S. market.
The new Ohio plant is expected to notably boost Honda's U.S. production and American-produced sales. Honda said nearly all of its vehicles sold in the U.S., including its Acura luxury brand, were produced in North America, including more than 60% in the U.S.
American Honda Motor Co. executive Jennifer Thomas recently emphasized the Japanese automaker's commitment to the U.S. and need for additional capacity.
"In order to be competitive in this market, you're going to need to build products here," Thomas, senior vice president of corporate affairs, said Oct. 27 in Detroit. "We are focused on trying to maximize the existing capacity that we have, but we are at capacity, and so we're exploring all options."
Thomas also warned the automotive industry faces a "catastrophic" scenario if the U.S. and Canada cannot reach a new trade deal by the end of this year, when Trump has threatened to double tariffs on Canadian vehicles and parts from 25% to 50% on Jan. 1 if the two countries don't reach a deal.
Honda said it has built more than 33 million vehicles and more than 39 million engines in the U.S. since it started auto production in the U.S. in 1982.
The Japanese automaker currently has more than 30,000 employees in the U.S.

articles.title_orig: Syria Signs Deal With China for 6.5 Million Prepaid Electricity Meters, Raising Questions Over Consumer Costs
articles.title_zh: Syria Signs Deal With China for 6.5 Million Prepaid Electricity Meters, Raising Questions Over Consumer Costs
articles.content_orig:
[DAMASCUS] The Syrian Electricity Company signed an agreement with Chinese company Wasion Group Limited on Sunday to supply 6.5 million prepaid smart electricity meters, as part of efforts to modernize electricity consumption monitoring and improve power grid management in Syria. The deal raises questions about its cost, financing arrangements, and potential impact on consumers’ electricity bills.
The agreement was signed at the Syrian Electricity Company’s headquarters in Damascus, in the presence of representatives from both the Syrian and Chinese sides, as part of a broader government plan to modernize the energy sector and introduce digital systems into electricity services.
The media office of the Syrian Electricity Company, which operates under the Ministry of Energy, told The Media Line that the agreement includes the supply of 6 million single-phase meters, primarily intended for residential properties and small businesses, along with 500,000 three-phase meters, typically used by commercial and industrial facilities requiring greater electrical capacity.
According to the media office, the agreement also includes software systems and technical equipment necessary to operate the meters, allowing for more accurate consumption measurements, improved customer data management, reduced electricity losses, and more efficient network monitoring.
The media office explained that the prepaid metering system requires consumers to purchase electricity credit before using power, rather than paying periodic bills based on consumption recorded after use.
The new system is expected to improve electricity bill collection, reduce errors associated with traditional meter readings, and enable subscribers to monitor their electricity consumption more accurately.

The official announcement did not disclose the financial value of the contract or specify who would bear the costs of purchasing and installing the meters. It also did not clarify whether subscribers would be required to pay fees to replace their existing meters or how the prepaid system would be implemented for low-income households.
Authorities have also not announced a specific timetable for delivering all the meters covered by the agreement or identified which governorates will be included in the initial phase of implementation.
Khaled Abu Di, director of the General Establishment for Electricity Transmission and Distribution, previously announced that the institution had developed a plan to replace conventional electricity meters with smart meters over approximately three years.
In January 2026, Abu Di revealed that around 1.2 million electricity subscribers in Syria still lacked electricity meters, highlighting the scale of the challenges involved in modernizing metering, billing, and revenue collection systems.
The agreement comes as Syria’s electricity sector continues to face significant challenges following years of war, including damage to power generation facilities and transmission and distribution networks, as well as the need for substantial investment to rehabilitate infrastructure and improve the reliability of electricity supplies.
Although introducing smart meters could improve consumption management and reduce commercial electricity losses, modernizing metering systems does not necessarily mean an increase in electricity generation or an end to power outages. Improving the number of hours electricity is available also requires upgrading power plants, transmission and distribution networks, and securing reliable energy supplies.
The prepaid nature of the new meters raises additional questions about their impact on Syrian households, particularly amid difficult economic conditions and concerns about consumers’ ability to regularly purchase electricity credit.
It also remains unclear whether the government intends to introduce changes to electricity tariffs alongside the new system or will limit the initiative to modernizing metering and payment collection procedures.
The agreement represents another step in economic and technological cooperation between Syria and China, as Damascus seeks to attract foreign companies to participate in rehabilitating public services and infrastructure.

articles.title_orig: As War Roils Energy Markets, China Sees Its Emissions Drop
articles.title_zh: As War Roils Energy Markets, China Sees Its Emissions Drop
articles.content_orig:
Rooftop solar in Chengdu, China. Pexels
China’s carbon dioxide emissions have been flat or falling for more than two years as renewables stunt demand for fossil fuels. But the country just saw its steepest quarterly drop since the Covid pandemic, thanks to energy shocks rippling from the Iran war.
Between July and September, China saw its carbon dioxide emissions fall by 3.1 percent, according to an analysis of official figures and commercial data by Carbon Brief . That is the biggest quarterly decline since the 2022 pandemic lockdowns.
The analysis finds oil use fell by 4 percent, year on year, as Chinese drivers flocked to electric vehicles at a time when the Iran war is driving up the cost of fuel. Electric cars accounted for two in three new passenger vehicles sold in China in September, according to industry data . The uptake of electric cars has helped China ramp down oil imports in the wake of the conflict, analysts find .
Emissions from coal, meanwhile, fell by 3 percent, year on year, as the rapid growth of renewables far outstripped the rise in power demand. China added enough wind, solar, and nuclear generation over the same period to power Germany and more than twice as much as needed to meet China’s growing demand. Emissions from the production of steel and concrete also fell amid the ongoing construction slowdown.
China is continuing to build new coal plants despite the decline in coal generation. As the number of generators grows and the use of coal power declines, the average plant is seeing its running hours drop.
The shift from coal to renewables comes even as large volumes of solar and wind power go unused. China is now generating much more clean electricity than its power grid can handle. In the first six months of this year, China rejected roughly a quarter of its wind and solar output.
Analysts say that China lacks the transmission infrastructure necessary to ferry abundant clean energy from where it is generated to where it is needed. Also at issue is a policy that guarantees the purchase of electricity from newly built coal power plants.

LONDON — Songmont, the Chinese brand that has made global headlines for cultural storytelling that resonates with China ‘s middle class, will launch its first footwear collection Wednesday.
Known for accessories that translate the landscapes, architecture and craft traditions of brand founder Fu Song’s hometown, Shanxi province, the brand is extending its offering beyond bags, ready-to-wear and fragrance with a footwear range inspired by the Wotou shoe.
Wotou is a traditional style named for its resemblance to a dome-shaped steamed corn bun popular in northern China . Traditionally handmade and padded with cotton, the model’s soft construction and distinctive raised seam informed Songmont’s contemporary interpretation for its debut footwear range.
The new silhouette launching this week, retailing for 2,680 renminbi, or $400, echoes the original, while piping joins two leather panels to recreate the ridge across the upper. Songmont’s tiger-tooth hardware adds a modern detail. The toe combines a square shape with softened edges, and layered leather forms a stepped heel inspired by Shanxi architecture. The style will come in 2.5cm and 6cm heel heights.
Songmont said it has spent more than a year developing the shoes, with 20-plus rounds of fittings and refinements. A custom last was designed to accommodate a range of foot shapes, and the use of full-grain cowhide uppers, a double-layer construction, sheepskin lining and high-resilience cotton insoles is meant to balance support, softness and breathability.
The brand added that the footwear launch builds on a design language it has developed across its collections. Its Gather bag, for example, recalls camel bags of the ancient Silk Road, while the Song bucket bag takes cues from traditional kite frameworks.
“As long as we choose things we genuinely like, the brand remains consistent. If we always chase trends or pay too much attention to what’s new, we can end up not knowing what we want,” Fu said about the brand’s approach in an earlier interview with WWD in Paris.
Founded in 2013, Songmont has around 20 stores in China and is expanding at a measured pace, with a focus on customer experience. It plans to open its first Hong Kong store in December, adding a new address as the brand continues to grow beyond mainland China.

Disney has lined up its next big AI partner, this time teaming with Adobe on a multi-year alliance to bring customized generative AI models into its creative pipelines across its businesses, including tools that will transform hand-drawn sketches into fully rendered concept art.
Under the terms of the agreement, Adobe will be Disney’s official “AI Innovation Partner” and will give the company access to Firefly, Firefly Foundry, Premiere, Photoshop, and dedicated engineering resources. Together, the companies will develop bespoke AI models trained on Disney IP to “generate commercially safe and production-ready outputs.”
According to the release , the work is already underway, with Walt Disney Imagineering using Firefly Foundry to generate 2D concept art from human-made drawings and create IP-based graphics for its parks development. Adobe will also work with Disney’s StudioLAB on experimental production workflows and ESPN Edge on AI-powered sports content.
The Adobe partnership is only the latest in a string of high-profile attempts by Disney to get ahead of the AI curve through corporate partnerships.
A year ago, Disney unveiled its most dramatic overhaul of Disney+ since the streamer’s launch, including a full-on embrace of generative AI tools for users. Then, in December, the company announced a $1 billion investment in OpenAI, a deal that collapsed when Sora was shut down and before any money changed hands.
More recently, Disney hired former Character.AI CEO Karandeep Anand as its first chief technology officer and committed roughly $180 million to recruiting employees from his former company, as it announced another major round of layoffs in a year largely defined by cuts across the company.
While the financial terms of the Adobe deal have not been made public, such a high-profile partnership once again shows where Disney’s priorities lie. Even as it eliminates thousands of jobs, demands further cost reductions, and commits billions to shareholder-benefiting stock buybacks, the company continues pouring resources into AI technologies that could fundamentally change how creative work is produced, and who gets paid to do it.

The rival leaders of the ethnically split island of Cyprus agreed on Monday to open two new crossing points for vehicular traffic along a U.N.-controlled buffer zone in the first such development in nearly a decade.
There are currently nine crossing points along the entire 180-kilometer (120-mile) length of the buffer zone that separates the breakaway Turkish Cypriot north from the Greek Cypriot south, where the internationally recognized government is seated.
Long lines of vehicles at some of these checkpoints have been a point of grievance for many, and it’s hoped that the two additional ones in the island’s northwest and southeast will help ease access for thousands who use them daily.
It’s not clear when the new crossing points will open but they will be launched simultaneously.
More notably, the agreement signifies tangible progress in talks between Greek Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman after months of discussions on trust-building measures that it's hoped will pave the way for a resumption of full-fledged negotiations to resolve the island’s ethnic divide.
Cyprus was split in 1974 when Turkey invaded after supporters of union with Greece mounted a coup backed by the Greek junta then ruling the country.
Turkish Cypriots declared independence in the island’s northern third in 1983, but only Turkey recognizes it and maintains more than 35,000 troops there.
María Ángela Holguín, the personal envoy of U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres for Cyprus, had warned in recent interviews to Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot media outlets that a resumption of formal peace talks would be unlikely if the two leaders didn't at least agree to new crossing points.
The announcement came after Christodoulides and Erhurman met with Holguín inside the buffer zone on the capital’s western outskirts. Christodoulides said that the results Thursday could have been “clearly better, more,” but underscored that real progress has been made.
Despite this, deep rifts remain between the two sides. Turkey and the Turkish Cypriots say the long-held, U.N.-endorsed formula to reunify Cyprus as a federation has been eclipsed and that the only “realistic” arrangement would be two separate states.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Thursday said that “it is time to accept the reality that there are two separate peoples and two separate states on the island,” and called on others to recognize the breakaway Turkish Cypriots, according to Turkey's Anadolu news agency.
Greek Cypriots reject any notion of formally partitioning the island as well as the key Turkish and Turkish Cypriot demands for a permanent, post-settlement Turkish military presence and military intervention rights ceded to Ankara that they see as existential threats.

articles.title_orig: Google Escalates Nvidia Rivalry With Specialized Versions of AI Chips
articles.title_zh: Google Escalates Nvidia Rivalry With Specialized Versions of AI Chips
articles.content_orig:
Google Cloud is expanding its TPU lineup with one chip for secure AI workloads and another for higher-capacity inference with large context windows.
To meet growing demand for AI inference, Google Cloud on Monday beefed up its Tensor Processing Unit family with two new chips: a more secure version of its TPU 8t accelerator and a higher-capacity version of its TPU 8i inference chip.
The new processors are designed to address two emerging enterprise requirements: stronger protection for sensitive AI workloads and better performance for agentic AI applications with large context windows, said Mark Lohmeyer, vice president and general manager of AI and computing infrastructure at Google Cloud.
The announcements build on Google Cloud’s eighth-generation TPU chips introduced in April. At that time, the company launched TPU 8t for training, which it said delivers up to 2.7 times better training performance than the prior generation, and TPU 8i for inference, which it said offers 80% better inference price-performance.
One of the new accelerators, TPU 8tx, is built on the same silicon as TPU 8t and adds hardware-level encryption for secure inference and small-scale training. The chip is paired with custom AMD CPU hosts to help protect and isolate sensitive data and model weights, even while inference is actively running, Lohmeyer said during a media briefing.
Related: Nvidia Probes Huang Ties as AI Industry Weighs the Fallout
Google Cloud also introduced TPU 8i Max, a variant aimed at enterprises running increasingly agentic workloads with large context windows. Lohmeyer said the chip is intended to address memory constraints by effectively “adding more lanes to the highway.”
To create TPU 8i Max, Google Cloud combined two TPU 8i chips into a single package, doubling compute, SRAM, and HBM bandwidth compared with TPU 8i, the company said. TPU 8i Max delivers 384 GB of high-bandwidth memory, Lohmeyer said.
“We’re just seeing tremendous demand for the TPU platform and systems,” Lohmeyer said during the briefing. He added that Google Cloud is also seeing a broadening of AI use cases, including demand for confidential computing and for agentic inference with very large context windows while maintaining strong performance.
Dave McCarthy, group vice president at IDC, said Google Cloud’s move toward more specialized custom AI chips could help it further differentiate itself from rival cloud providers.
“The fact that Google was able to launch the 8i and 8t earlier this year, and now they’re coming out with these new ones within the same calendar year, is just showing the pace of innovation,” McCarthy said. “They’re showing their commitment to R&D to build this stuff. And if what they’re saying is true – twice the bandwidth, all these new features – that’s showing they’re potentially outpacing the competition in terms of new product releases.”
Related: Nvidia, AMD Commit $4B to Meta AI Buildout
McCarthy described confidential computing as an emerging requirement for AI workloads. Cloud providers have traditionally focused on protecting data in transit and at rest, he said, whereas confidential computing is intended to protect data in use.
“If Google can come out with a strong confidential compute story, it kind of gives them a little bit of an edge,” said McCarthy, adding that Nvidia is still developing its strategy in this area.
Google Cloud also said TPU 8i Max allows more silicon to fit within an existing rack footprint, enabling significantly more computing power per square foot and per watt in its data centers.
That could help Google Cloud increase capacity without adding more racks or building more data centers, at least in the near term, potentially easing some of the capacity pressures facing the industry, McCarthy said.
More broadly, McCarthy said Google Cloud’s strategy of continually enhancing its silicon and making TPUs available through other providers could expand the company’s market reach while creating an additional revenue stream.
Related: Oracle Cloud to Offer Google TPUs and New AI Chips
Oracle recently announced it would make TPU chips available to customers of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. During the media briefing, Lohmeyer also said Google Cloud would allow select customers to deploy the TPU 8tx in their own data centers.

Federal safety regulators are investigating Waymo self-driving cars after reports that the robo-taxis illegally pass school buses — even after a software update last year that was intended to solve the issue.
The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said Monday it opened a recall query into 2,895 vehicles over the continued safety violations, according to Reuters.
The investigation will determine whether a software update Waymo issued under a December 2025 recall fixed the issue — or whethe r Waymo vehicles still pass school buses with flashing red lights or extended stop arms, indicating that vehicles behind them cannot pass.
It is illegal in all 50 U.S. states to pass a stopped school bus.
The auto regulator opened a “recall query” to “assess the adequacy” of Waymo’s initial remedy.
The administration claims the majority of incidents involving Waymo vehicles passing school buses occurred after November 2025, when Waymo said it had completed the software update necessary to fix the issue.
The feds also opened a probe into the company in January after one of the self-driving vehicles hit a child near an elementary school in Santa Monica, California, as the child was heading to school.
The child sustained “minor injuries” from the incident, the company said at the time.
Months later, in October, the administration launched a preliminary probe into Waymo after reports emerged of the autonomous cars not following traffic laws near school buses.
Austin Independent School District in Texas reported 24 alleged violations by Waymo cars as of January, a spokesperson told The Independent at the time.
Incidents of Waymo cars passing stopped school buses were also reported in Atlanta.
As a result, Waymo announced a voluntary software recall in December of last year for over 3,000 vehicles. While the company said the update had been fully deployed, the administration’s probe will look into the adequacy of the remedy.
Waymo currently has fleets in several major U.S. cities, including Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Atlanta, Orlando, Miami and Austin, Texas.

articles.title_orig: KFC’s arrival at Italian ski slopes angers food and mountain purists
articles.title_zh: KFC’s arrival at Italian ski slopes angers food and mountain purists
articles.content_orig:
Fast-food outlets at two prestigious Dolomites resorts are Italy’s first, with legal action threatened
Europe live – latest updates
Skiers on the slopes of two of Italy’s most prestigious resorts will be able to dine from buckets of fried chicken between runs this winter as the US fast-food chain KFC prepares to open outlets, infuriating mountain and food purists while prompting a prominent businessman to threaten legal action.
KFC will open its first high-altitude restaurants on the slopes of Cortina d’Ampezzo and Madonna di Campiglio, in the Dolomites, on 5 December, an initiative the company said was aimed at “surprising people” and “reaching places” where nobody would expect to find it.
The move marks a debut for any fast-food outlet on an Italian ski slope, bringing a menu replete with KFC’s most popular products, from spicy wings and burgers to traditional buckets of fried chicken.
The plans appear to have taken people by surprise, not least Alberico Zardini, a majority shareholder in Faloria Spa, the company that manages the infrastructure on Mount Faloria in Cortina d’Ampezzo, where there is to be a KFC at 2,123 metres.
“The mere idea is disgraceful,” Zardini told Il Messaggero . “It’s absurd and shameful to imagine a fast-food joint in the most beautiful spot in Cortina. Do the people of Cortina not realise what we’re risking here?”
Zardini said he had written to the bosses of Faloria warning that he would pursue legal action unless they put the brakes on KFC’s mountain ambitions.
He said it was “a mad decision”, especially because the outlet would be selling fried chicken inside the Faloria mountain club, where a luxury lodge is due to open on an upper floor. “I am 100% against it and will not just sit back and watch,” he said.
The KFC in Madonna di Campiglio, in south-western Trentino on the opposite side of the Dolomites, will be at 1,700 metres on Piana di Nambino, next door to a swish après-ski club.
The two outlets came under the fast food chain’s “quick service restaurants” product range and were the company’s way of targeting a broader market beyond its loyal Gen Z customers, “from young families to mountain lovers”, said Marzia Farè, the chief marketing officer for KFC Italia.
“We strongly wanted this project because it perfectly represents the way we imagine the evolution of KFC: continuing to surprise, reaching places where no one would expect to find us, and doing so without giving up what makes us unique,” she told brandnews.it .
after newsletter promotion
Needless to say, with the cost of ski passes in Italy increasing each year, the outlets will appeal to those looking for cheap food in otherwise extremely pricey resorts.
But Oscar Farinetti, the founder of Eataly, Italy’s high-end food-store chain, has said the brand “doesn’t belong here at all” – while pointing the blame at customers. “We Italian consumers should be a tad more cultured,” he told Il Sole 24 Ore . “We need to acknowledge our assets – our cuisine made of few ingredients and excellent products. There is a lack of studying one’s own roots – we’re eating fried chicken instead of a nice slice of salami with a glass of fresh wine.”
Luigi Casanova from Mountain Wilderness, an NGO that works to protect mountain environments, told Corriere della Sera : “The era of polenta and luganega sausage is over,” while Paola Demagri, from Trentino’s provincial council, spoke about mountain identity being “sold out to Kentucky chicken”.
Others were more measured in their response. Cristian Ferrari, the president of Società Alpinisti Tridentini, the oldest mountain association in the Trentino area, said: “We have nothing against fried chicken, but are we sure this is the issue we should be most worried about?”

articles.title_orig: Thick smog shrouds New Delhi after Diwali firecrackers add to seasonal pollution
articles.title_zh: Thick smog shrouds New Delhi after Diwali firecrackers add to seasonal pollution
articles.content_orig:
People walk in front of India Gate, shrouded in thick smog after firecrackers lit up the sky overnight during Diwali celebrations, in New Delhi, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. Manish Swarup/AP hide caption
NEW DELHI — A thick blanket of smog shrouded India's capital Monday after firecrackers lit up the skies over New Delhi during Diwali celebrations, compounding dangerously high pollution levels and intensifying the seasonal air pollution crisis that grips the city every year.
Despite restrictions on fireworks, residents in New Delhi celebrated the Hindu festival of lights with firecrackers on Sunday evening, releasing smoke and fine particulate matter into the atmosphere. The air quality index exceeded 350 in several parts of the capital on Monday morning, reaching the severe category and posing significant health risks.
Monitoring stations across the city recorded similarly alarming levels, while visibility deteriorated as a gray haze blanketed streets and high-rise buildings.
India's Supreme Court in October had sought to limit Diwali pollution by restricting conventional firecrackers and allowing only approved "green firecrackers" under specified conditions for three-hour windows on Saturday and Sunday. The crackers produce fewer emissions but are not pollution-free. They still release particulate matter and other pollutants, adding to the city's already hazardous air.
Isyad, a New Delhi resident who uses one name, said the worsening smog was taking a toll on his health.
"Because of the pollution there is irritation in the throat and itching in the eyes," he said.
New Delhi and its metropolitan region, home to more than 30 million people, regularly rank among the world's most polluted areas during winter. Pollution worsens as Diwali fireworks coincide with cooler weather and smoke from crop-residue fires in neighboring states of Punjab and Haryana.
After harvesting rice, farmers often burn leftover stalks to clear their fields for the next planting season. The smoke drifts toward New Delhi, adding to pollution from vehicles, industries, construction dust and other local sources.
The problem becomes particularly acute in late October and November, when cooler temperatures, low wind speeds and stagnant atmospheric conditions prevent pollutants from dispersing. The result is a thick haze that can linger over the capital and surrounding areas for days.
People walk through thick smog after firecrackers lit up the sky overnight during Diwali celebrations in New Delhi, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. Manish Swarup/AP hide caption
Authorities in New Delhi have implemented a set of measures to curb pollution, which include limits on construction activity and restrictions on diesel generators, while courts have sough restrictions on firecrackers. But the measures have not prevented the return of severe pollution each year.
Environmentalists say long-term solutions, such as cleaner energy and stricter controls on vehicle emissions, are needed to prevent the annual crisis.
Shweta Narayan, a public health expert at the Global Climate and Health Alliance, described the government's response so far as "knee-jerk" and "temporary."
"A lot of interventions happen only because the government is pressured or pushed in a corner to do something," she said.

articles.title_orig: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
articles.title_zh: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
articles.content_orig:
Resident birds have returned to Broughshane Waterfowl Park after an oil spill which caused the death of 13 of the flock.
The popular attraction in County Antrim was forced to close after a nearby home heating oil tank was vandalised , causing the oil spill into the pond.
In a post on social media, The Waterfowl Pond confirmed that work is still underway to address the oil contamination and that a number of pens remain out of bounds.
More than 20 birds were transported to the USPCA's headquarters for urgent specialist care following the incident.
The park, which was home to 120 birds, has since reopened.
Broughshane Environment Wildfowl and Wildlife Trust's chairman, Gary Hayward, said about 10-12 birds have returned including two black swans and Nenes.
Hayward said they are back safely in their pens and they are lucky to be healthy.
The Northern Ireland Environment Agency (NIEA) was first alerted to the incident on Thursday 22 October and have been involved in removing the oil waste.
The agency said the substance involved had been identified as home heating oil or kerosene.
Police said about 44 gallons (200 litres) of oil had leaked from the tank which had been damaged at a business premise in the Main Street area of Broughshane.
Hayward said that there is very little evidence of the oil left as the NIEA have removed the majority of it.
"They have made problems a lot less than they could have been," he told BBC News NI.
He said there is still some oil around the edges, and once the oil leaves the pens the birds will be moved back into them.
The USPCA has also been a key part of the rescue operation.
They said that all of the birds, including geese, ducks and swans, needed bathed and treated due to the level of contamination they suffered.
Unfortunately some had already ingested too much and died as a result.
The Waterfowl Pond offered thanks to the USPCA for looking after the birds.
"We are truly grateful for everything you have done."
It also paid tribute to the support received from the public.
"It's another positive step forward for our park, and we couldn't have got here without you."
Police have said that enquiries into the incident are ongoing and have appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

articles.title_orig: Leaker Envisions a Shorter iPhone With a New iOS Layout
articles.title_zh: Leaker Envisions a Shorter iPhone With a New iOS Layout
articles.content_orig:
A future iPhone could keep its current width while becoming shorter, with iOS preserving room for content by moving some controls into the status bar, in a theory shared by the Weibo leaker known as " Instant Digital ."
Instant Digital imagines Apple shortening a non-folding iPhone once its display has only a single camera cutout or the front-facing camera moves entirely beneath the screen. Taking roughly a status bar's worth of height off the display would bring its aspect ratio from around 19.5:9 to closer to 18:9, apparently making the phone easier to hold and use with one hand.
Controls that currently sit below the status bar could share a row with the time and system indicators. Instant Digital's idea is that combining the two rows would let the shorter display show the same amount of information. The leaker described the layout and proportions as personal speculation.
Apple has already changed how iOS uses the space at the top of the screen with the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo . The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌'s smaller Dynamic Island supports up to three simultaneous Live Activities, up from two on earlier models. On the ‌iPhone Duo‌, iOS fits a compact status bar into the corner and positions the Dynamic Island vertically along the side of the outer display.
The timing of a cutout-free display on the iPhone remains uncertain. The leaker "Digital Chat Station" has said Apple is testing under-display camera technology and has described an intermediate design  with a visible hole for the front-facing camera, similar to the ‌iPhone Duo‌.
In a follow-up post on Weibo , another user said they expect iPhones to retain a camera cutout and a 19.5:9 aspect ratio in both 2027 and 2028. Instant Digital replied that some sources say the cutout could disappear in 2028. Display analyst Ross Young has separately said he expects the 2028 iPhone Pro models to retain a centered camera cutout.
In a separate post , Instant Digital said they had a growing hunch that iOS would change substantially after the 20th-anniversary iPhone launches in 2027. They expect changes to how users interact with the software as well as how it looks.
Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman reported that the anniversary iPhone will have curved glass and thinner bezels in the biggest overhaul to the Pro line since the iPhone X. Digital Chat Station has also said Apple was testing a roughly 7-inch display for the largest anniversary model with the same aspect ratio as the iPhone 17 Pro Max.
The iPhone X offers a precedent for a hardware redesign changing how people use iOS. When Apple removed the Home button in 2017, iOS 11 introduced swipe-up navigation on the iPhone X.

articles.title_orig: What Hardware Does Your PC Need To Run A Local AI Model?
articles.title_zh: What Hardware Does Your PC Need To Run A Local AI Model?
articles.content_orig:
I've been a staunch proponent of self-hosting AI for a while now, and the points that I usually make are centered around data privacy and the fiscal cost of self-hosting your own models versus paying for a monthly subscription.
One of the most frequent comments I get says that whatever I save by self-hosting my models is offset by my power bill, which always felt hyperbolic. To find out exactly how much local AI inference adds to my power bill each month, I benchmarked a model with llama-bench, the benchmark tool built into llama.cpp, logged power draw with HWiNFO and Nvidia's own nvidia-smi on my RTX 4070 Ti Super PC, and found that the cost is nowhere close to what I'd pay for a single AI subscription. Here is what I found, and how I measured it.
To make the test and an estimation of cost as comprehensive as possible, I picked Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, which is a model that's too big for my RTX 4070 Ti Super's 16GB of GDDR6X memory on its own, and not lacking in capability at any task I throw at it.
At 16.5GB in its UD-IQ4_XS quantization, I tend to offload the experts from eight of its layers to my Ryzen 5 7600X with llama.cpp's --n-cpu-moe flag to get a comfortable inference speed. This also puts the CPU to work on every token generated by the model, so measuring the GPU alone would have concealed a big part of the power bill, which is exactly why I accounted for the CPU in the cost accounting as well.
I used llama-bench , which is a benchmark test that comes baked into llama.cpp (build b11927) to time the two jobs a model does, which is reading prompts and generating tokens. For this test, I gave the model a 2,048 token prompt to read ten times over and instructed it to generate 512 tokens five times over, both starting from an empty context.
While llama-bench ran, I used HWiNFO to log the CPU's package power and nvidia-smi to log the GPU's board power every half a second. Added together, the two peaked at 237.5W while reading and 251.9W while generating.
Then, I took an approach that can be described as hyperbolic in the accounting of costs, which entailed stacking the deck against myself. I priced every token as if my CPU and GPU drew that peak for the entire run, did not subtract their idle draw, and used the U.S. Energy Information Administration's 2026 projected average U.S. residential rate of 18.2 cents per kWh .
The rest of the system, including the RAM, the fans, and power supply losses wasn't logged by HWiNFO, so I'll show what another 100W on top does, which is the figure I would use as the true "worst case."
Cost per million tokens (USD)
To put that in context, or more aptly, in subscription terms, $20 buys about 110 kWh at the currently projected U.S. average rate. At my measured peak of 251.9W, my PC would have to generate tokens non-stop for roughly 436 hours to burn through that, which works out to about 14.5 hours a day, every day, for a month.
Even with the extra 100W on top, it still comes to around 312 hours, or over 10 hours a day. That's counting generation alone, which is the expensive half of the process, since reading a prompt costs well under a cent per million tokens even if you were to consider the worst case.
At this point, you would've likely realized that comparing the cost of running a local model versus paying for a cloud-based subscription service is quite a ridiculous practice. However, there's one final bit of accounting left, and that's comparing the two.
When you pay for a monthly subscription service, the price of each token remains hidden, but the API rate cards from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI don't, which makes them the most fitting standard of measure for what a model's output is worth. I compiled their list prices against my measured numbers for a clear comparison.
Input (per million tokens, USD)
Output (per million tokens, USD)
Output vs Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on RTX 4070 Ti S
67x (Introductory pricing)
There are a lot of misconceptions surrounding the cost of running local models on the hardware you own, particularly relating to power draw. Part of what feeds into these misconceptions is the fact that a GPU running close to its rated power looks and feels energy-intensive, so most people assume that a model keeps the GPU pinned to that figure as long as it's running. However, that is rarely ever the case, because token generation leans on memory more than raw compute.
My RTX 4070 Ti Super peaked at 144W while generating and 177W while reading a prompt against its 285W rating, and even with the CPU's draw and an extra 100W on top, I'd have to keep the model generating continuously for over 10 hours a day before it could match one $20 AI subscription.

articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that he was ordering the Justice Department to investigate Democratic leaders over what he described as threats against Republican officials, donors and supporters, without identifying the alleged communications or providing evidence of criminal conduct.
"The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people, including the Attorney General of the United States, and others, with Impeachment and many other forms of punishment, even though they admit they have no reason to do so," Trump said in a Truth Social post .
The alleged threats, the president said, are "extortion at the highest level," he wrote. "I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!"
In his post, Trump claimed that Democratic Sen. Elissa Slotkin of Michigan is planning to "go after all young people that believe in Republican Values."
Trump was apparently referencing a speech Slotkin made at a University of Chicago event on Oct. 13. At the time, Slotkin said: "I want young people coming out of school to say, 'Should I go work for the Trump administration?'...I want them to be like, 'Lord, that might be buying myself a ton of problems that I don't want. And so let me avoid participating in that.' I want that deterrence message sent."
Slotkin alleges that she, her family and her staff faced physical and legal intimidation after the posting of a November 2025 video in which Slotkin and other Democratic leaders called on the U.S. military to "refuse illegal orders" following the airstrikes targeting boats in the Caribbean.
On Nov. 20, Trump called the video treason and said "an example must be set."
The FBI contacted lawmakers, including Slotkin, days later. In February, Slotkin declined to sit for an interview the Justice Department requested about the video.
"The intimidation is the point, and I'm not gonna go along with that," the senator said in February. A federal grand jury later declined to indict the video participants.
Now, Trump alleges Democrats are threatening legal intimidation against Republican leaders and their supporters.
"Republicans should get smart, fast! Threatening letters have been sent to many people, all innocent, from Democrat Political Leaders," the president wrote.
The White House and Slotkin didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

articles.title_orig: iPhone 18e Could Feature Bigger Display and Battery
articles.title_zh: iPhone 18e Could Feature Bigger Display and Battery
articles.content_orig:
Apple's standard iPhone 18 and the lower-cost iPhone 18e will both feature 6.3-inch displays and use the same battery, according to the leaker known as " Fixed Focus Digital ."
In a new post on Weibo, the leaker shared an annotated, side-by-side diagram of the phones' purported internals, labeled "Taycan" for the ‌iPhone 18‌ and "Nevera" for the iPhone 18e. Fixed Focus Digital said the diagram was already circulating online and broadly matched what their sources had told them. They pointed to the battery as an example of the interchangeable parts they had previously described.
The diagram's annotations list a 4,430 mAh battery for both models. That would be an increase of about 21% from 3,671 mAh for the standard ‌iPhone 18‌ and about 11% from 4,005 mAh for the iPhone 18e. The notes attribute the extra room in the standard model to changes to the bottom speaker and haptic engine. The diagram also shows two rear cameras on the standard ‌iPhone 18‌, including an Ultra Wide camera, and a single rear camera on the iPhone 18e, just like previous models.
A 6.3-inch display would be a noticeable step up from the 6.1-inch screen on the iPhone 17e . Fellow Weibo leaker "Digital Chat Station" previously claimed the iPhone 18e would retain a 6.12-inch OLED display at 60Hz , along with a single 48-megapixel rear camera and a potential upgrade to the front-facing camera. The same source expects the standard iPhone 18 to retain its 6.3-inch display with a refresh rate of up to 120Hz, along with a larger battery.
In an earlier post , Fixed Focus Digital said a new chip was the only iPhone 18e upgrade they could confirm at the time and suggested the two models would share some manufacturing processes.
Digital Chat Station expects the iPhone 18e to contain Apple's 2nm A20 chip, up from the 3nm A19 in the ‌iPhone 17e‌. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo has said Apple's lower-end spring 2027 iPhones will pair the A20 chip with 9GB of RAM , up from 8GB. Both models are also rumored to get Apple's C2 modem, which would replace the Snapdragon X80 in the iPhone 17 and the C1X in the ‌iPhone 17e‌.
The iPhone 18e is expected to launch in spring 2027 alongside the standard ‌iPhone 18‌ and second-generation iPhone Air . The ‌iPhone 17e‌ launched at $599 with 256GB of storage , and it is unclear if it will get a price increase like other iPhone models.

articles.title_zh: Nvidia, Palantir, and Tesla Are Sending Shockwaves Through Wall Street With This $53 Billion Warning
articles.content_orig:
For the better part of the last four years, no catalyst has played a bigger role in lifting the broader market than the evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) . Whether it's AI-accelerating hardware or AI applications, an IDC report pegs this cumulative addressable opportunity at $22.5 trillion from 2025 to 2031.
Few companies have taken the AI bull by the horns more than Nvidia ( NVDA +2.77% ) , Palantir Technologies ( PLTR +3.48% ) , and Tesla ( TSLA +4.23% ) .
Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) are the infrastructure backbone of AI-accelerated data centers. None of its competitors are particularly close to matching the compute capabilities of its multiple generations of GPUs.
Meanwhile, AI-driven software-as-a-service provider Palantir is a veritable blueprint for deploying AI applications. The company's Gotham platform assists the U.S. military with planning and overseeing missions.
Electric-vehicle maker Tesla is also an AI applications maven. AI is integral to the success of its full self-driving software and its Optimus humanoid robots.
Image source: Getty Images.
While this trio has thrived amid the AI infrastructure build-out, the individuals who know these companies best are sending all the wrong signals to Wall Street .
Though stock market analysts spend day after day studying the same industry and the companies that define it, no one understands Nvidia, Palantir, and Tesla better than their respective insiders.
An " insider " is a high-ranking executive, board member, or beneficial owner of at least 10% of a company's outstanding shares who may possess nonpublic information. Anytime an insider buys or sells their company's stock, they're legally required to file Form 4 with regulators within two business days. This allows investors to track whether a company's insiders have been buying or selling.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/06/26
In the case of this powerhouse AI trio, insiders have been undeniable net sellers of their company's stock over the trailing five years:
Collectively, insiders at these companies have sold more than $52.7 billion more of their own company's stock than they've purchased since early November 2021.
There is, however, an asterisk that should accompany the above data. Since high-ranking executives and board members are often compensated in stock or options , they're required to sell some of their holdings to cover their federal and/or state tax liability. In other words, insider selling isn't automatically a bad thing -- especially if it's for tax purposes.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/06/26
What's equally unnerving, from an investment standpoint, is the relative lack of insider buying . With the exception of one sizable purchase totaling nearly $1 billion by Tesla CEO Elon Musk, insider buying has been practically nonexistent in this trio over the trailing five years:
If insiders aren't buying, historical precedent might explain why.
For more than 30 years, every game-changing innovation has navigated an early-innings bubble-bursting event. This includes the internet, 3D printing, blockchain technology, and the metaverse.
Stock market bubbles throughout history…

AI stocks now ~40% of the market. https://t.co/RxSAh09k6F
The reason these bubbles form and subsequently burst is that investors consistently overestimate the pace of optimization for game-changing technologies . While AI solutions have been welcomed with open arms, we're likely several years away from businesses optimizing these solutions to boost sales and profits. In other words, the door is wide open for a potential AI bubble-bursting event.

articles.title_zh: Chinese zero tariff rule boosts South African apples
articles.content_orig:
By Fred Meintjes 2026-11-09T11:11:00+00:00
Tru-Cape says China’s new tariff deal for Africa is already benefitting South African exporters
The South African fruit business has said that while it has been able to grow exports to China under the country’s zero tariff deal for African countries, there is a short window of opportunity for it to negotiate a permanent trade deal.
The country’s apple exporters revealed this week that they have seen a significant increase in shipments to China.
“The removal of Chinese import tariffs on South African fruit is already delivering results for Tru-Cape Fruit Marketing, with the company’s apple exports to China increasing by almost 50 per cent year-to-date,” stated Tru-Cape Marketing.
”The development has created new opportunities to grow South African apples’ presence in one of the world’s largest consumer markets, while highlighting the need for more competitive market access in India.”
Previously, South African fruit entering China was subject to a 10 per cent import tariff.
The reduction to 0 per cent has levelled the playing field for Southern Hemisphere suppliers, giving South African exporters a more competitive position in the market.
This is likely to also provide further impetus for South African pear, table grape, stonefruit and citrus exporters.
“It is important that we secure a longer-term free trade agreements deal,” the Citrus Growers Association recently commented.
“The playing field is now definitely level, with all Southern Hemisphere countries enjoying a zero tariff,” noted Conrad Fick, marketing director at Tru-Cape.
Tru-Cape currently accounts for more than 20 per cent of South African apple exports to the market.
”South African Royal Gala Red and Royal Beaut apples are performing particularly well, and we are also seeing growing acceptance of the Flash Gala brand, which is helping to increase both volumes and prices,” said Fick.
The country’s stonefruit exporters are also looking forward to their first season in the Chinese market.
“We are particularly excited about building with Sugar Prunes which is already well accepted amongst Chinese consumers,” added Luhan Marais of Icon Fruit.
